description: Editorial description of the on-screen teaching sequence; not spoken narration. The soundtrack is music.

segments.text: A CNN maps pixels to a prediction, measures its error and updates its weights. The animation follows an image of the digit seven.
The input is a 12 by 12, single-channel grid. Pixel values describe brightness; intermediate values can represent softer edges.
A 3 by 3 filter contains nine learned weights and a bias. It starts with initial values, which training can change.
Convolution slides the same filter across the image. At each location, multiply corresponding pixels and weights, add the results and the bias, and write one output value.
Several filters produce several feature maps. Different learned filters can respond to different patterns.
ReLU replaces negative feature values with zero and keeps positive values.
Max pooling keeps the largest value from each small region, reducing spatial dimensions.
The illustrated path is 12×12×1 → 10×10×4 → 5×5×4 → 3×3×8. Deeper features combine information from a wider input region.
Flattening rearranges the 3×3×8 feature tensor into 72 values, preserving the values in a fixed ordering.
The dense classifier combines those features to produce scores for ten digits.
Softmax converts scores into nonnegative probabilities that sum to one. The largest probability is the current prediction.
Cross-entropy penalizes low probability for the true class. For a true-class probability of 0.205, the natural-log loss is approximately 1.585.
Backpropagation applies the chain rule through the classifier and feature extractor to calculate parameter gradients.
Gradient descent updates weights by subtracting learning rate times gradient.
Repeating prediction, loss, backpropagation and update over training examples can improve predictions. Evaluate on held-out data to check generalization.
